title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DOM'S BOWL
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Dom Ferrante, a twenty-seven-year-old window washer in Rochester, New York.
Dom hangs off twenty-story buildings and is not afraid of heights.
He is afraid of one thing. His grandmother, Nonna Lucia.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BROKEN BOWL
segments.quote: The way to love anything is to realize that it might be lost.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: One Sunday, Dom knocked Nonna's old pasta bowl off the counter. Sixty years old. A hundred pieces.
He had never looked at that bowl twice. Now Nonna swept it up very quietly.
His sister Gina had a G. K. Chesterton line on the fridge:
The way to love anything is to realize that it might be lost.
Nonna turns ninety in March. Dom signed up for a pottery class.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE EXPERT
segments.quote: In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities, but in the expert's there are few.
segments.author: Shunryu Suzuki
lines: Everyone in the Tuesday class was over seventy. Dom said he'd watched videos. He had this.
His first lump of clay flew off the wheel and hit the teacher, Harold, in the chest.
Harold wiped his shirt and quoted Shunryu Suzuki, a Zen teacher:
In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities, but in the expert's there are few.
So Dom stopped talking and watched Harold's hands.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: GIN RUMMY
segments.author: Miguel de Cervantes
lines: Dom ran the wheel full speed. Every bowl flopped over like a tired hat.
At the break, Mrs. Albright dealt gin rummy and quoted Cervantes:
Patience and shuffle the cards.
She won every hand. So Dom slowed the wheel down. The next bowl stood up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: FORTY BOWLS
segments.author: Sophocles
lines: It was lopsided. So was the next one.
Above the kiln, Harold had taped a line from Sophocles, the old Greek playwright:
Without labor nothing prospers.
So Dom came in every Saturday and made forty bowls. His mom now owns thirty-nine ugly bowls.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE KILN
segments.quote: He who fears he shall suffer, already suffers what he fears.
segments.author: Michel de Montaigne
lines: Bowl number forty was the one. He painted a little lemon on it, for Nonna's lemon tree.
But bowls can crack in the kiln. Dom couldn't sleep for two nights.
Harold laughed and quoted Montaigne, the French writer:
He who fears he shall suffer, already suffers what he fears.
So Dom went back to washing windows. The bowl came out whole.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: NONNA'S NINETIETH
segments.quote: Where there is great love there are always miracles.
segments.author: Willa Cather
lines: At the party, Dom handed Nonna the bowl. It leaned a little to the left.
Nonna cried, then told him a secret. Grandpa Sal made the old bowl at a night class in nineteen sixty-four. It leaned too.
Gina whispered a Willa Cather line:
Where there is great love there are always miracles.
Nonna filled it with pasta, and Dom signed up for spring.

segments.head: SIX WISE WORDS
segments.quote: Notice. Listen. Slow down. Keep at it. Stop worrying. Love.
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: So notice what you love, listen like a beginner, slow down, keep at it, stop worrying, and make something for someone.
Me? I once made a clay ashtray. My wife keeps her car keys in it.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
